interactions.summary: Jiang closes the family-loyalty discussion by saying the highest faith, hope, and love in Dante's world may require leaving one's family behind for justice.
A student reads the Minotaur passage, and Jiang pauses only to identify the Theseus reference before returning to the narrative.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student reading with brief Jiang gloss

interactions.summary: The reading moves from the shattered descent into the river of blood, introduces the centaurs who guard violent souls, and has Chiron assign Nessus as Dante's guide.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang's label 'the monitor' is a noisy ASR rendering of the Minotaur; his point is simply to flag a mythological reference rather than build an interpretation yet.

claims.claim: Jiang says that in Dante's historical world the greatest act of faith, hope, and love may be leaving family behind and trusting God to support a life of justice.
The canto descent is staged through the Minotaur and a shattered path whose collapse Virgil links to the cosmic shock around Christ's harrowing of hell.
Jiang identifies Theseus as the mythic killer of the Minotaur and treats the allusion as narrative machinery rather than a major interpretive hinge.
The reading presents the river of blood as the place where violent tyrants boil while centaurs police the boundary with arrows.

signature_moments.moment: The path of faith may require leaving behind the only support system you have.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the greatest act of faith, hope, and love at this time in history is to leave your family behind
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives Jiang's Dante a radical anti-tribal ethic rather than a merely pious one.

signature_moments.moment: Violence appears as a valley of blood patrolled by centaurs with arrows.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the stream of blood, where those who injure others violently boil
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's defining image and sets up Jiang's later argument about violent empire.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The beast guarding the violent descent in Canto 12, briefly glossed by Jiang through the Theseus myth.
The centaur leader who recognizes Dante as living and assigns Nessus to guide him through the ditch of blood.

chronology_notes.note: This packet closes the usury-and-family thread and then re-enters close reading at the literal descent into the first ring of violence.

uncertainty_notes.note: Some proper nouns in the read-aloud passage are ASR-noisy, but the structural move into the blood river and centaur guard is clear.
